layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract. Promoting the connectivity of curvilinear structures, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neuronal processes in biomedical scans and blood vessels in CT images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remains a key challenge in semantic segmentation. Traditional pixel-wise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss functions, including cross-entropy and Dice losses, often fail to cap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture high-level topological connectivity, resulting in topological mistakes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in graphs obtained from prediction maps. In this paper, we propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAPE (Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement), a novel loss function

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designed to enforce connectivity in graphs obtained from segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps by optimizing a graph connectivity metric. CAPE uses the graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representation of the ground truth to select node pairs and determine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their corresponding paths within the predicted segmentation through a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shortest-path algorithm. Using this, we penalize both disconnections and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: false positive connections, effectively promoting the model to preserve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological correctness. Experiments on 2D and 3D datasets, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neuron and blood vessel tracing demonstrate that CAPE significantly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improves topology-aware metrics and outperforms state-of-the-art meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods. Code is available at https://github.com/NeuraVisionLab/CAPE.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Keywords: Segmentation · Topology Optimization · Biomedical Imag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing · Neuronal Process Tracing · Blood Vessel Segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmenting curvilinear structures—such as neuronal processes in biomedical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scans and blood vessels in CT images—is essential for numerous applications in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical imaging and biological research. Traditional deep convolutional networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have significantly improved pixel-level segmentation. However, despite these ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vancements, they exhibit a fundamental limitation: they are trained using pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wise loss functions such as cross-entropy, Dice, or Mean Squared Error (MSE),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which do not explicitly enforce topological correctness, because they are de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signed to optimize the number of correctly segmented pixels/voxels, but do not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: account for high-level structural continuity. This is particularly problematic, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 大

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Corresponding author: doruk.oner@bilkent.edu.tr

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Esmaeilzadeh et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity errors can severely compromise the reliability of constructions and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their usability in downstream tasks. As a result, annotators are often required to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manually correct topological errors, a highly labor-intensive and tedious process,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially when dealing with large volumetric datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent approaches have focused on designing loss functions specifically aimed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at enforcing topological connectivity [16,4,10,3,2,22,18,19]. Some methods ana-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lyze the structural topology using Persistent Homology [4,10,3,2], while oth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ers incorporate perceptual loss by leveraging pre-trained feature extractors [16].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Additionally, certain approaches promote connectivity by enforcing background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separation through Rand index optimization [18,19]. Another strategy involves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: developing differentiable loss functions based on existing metrics [22]. Despite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these efforts, all existing methods attempt to achieve global connectivity by op-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: timizing a metric that is not explicitly designed for connectivity. Consequently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they only indirectly enforce the global topological correctness of predictions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose CAPE (Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement), a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: novel loss function that improves the connectivity of curvilinear structure recon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structions. Inspired by the Average Path Length Similarity (APLS) metric [5],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAPE evaluates connectivity by comparing entire paths instead of individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels. Specifically, it leverages Dijkstra's algorithm to compute shortest paths

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the pixel domain by mapping paths between nodes from the ground truth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: graph onto the predicted segmentation. This direct comparison enforces high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level topological correctness, leading to improved segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Over the years, various approaches have been proposed for delineating curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures, ranging from hand-designed filters [6,13,26] to learned filters [30,1]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using support vector machines [11], gradient boosting [24], and decision trees

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [27]. However, these traditional methods suffer from limited generalizability and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various shortcomings. With the advancements in deep learning, more powerful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deep neural networks have largely replaced these techniques [15,8,14,20,9,29].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent advances in biomedical image segmentation have been driven by deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional neural networks, with U-Net [21] being especially influential. While

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net achieves high pixel-level accuracy, conventional pixel-wise loss functions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neglect topological correctness—a critical issue for curvilinear structures like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neuronal processes, where connectivity errors degrade segmentation quality. Con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sequently, many studies have explored methods beyond pixel-wise losses to fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: harness the potential of deep networks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Several studies have designed novel topology-aware loss functions to improve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation performance of deep networks. [16] penalized differences in label

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and prediction feature maps using a pretrained VGG19 network [23], but it lacks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explicit topological preservation. Persistent Homology-based methods [4,10,3]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide differentiable topological similarity but ignore spatial alignment, lead-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing to inaccuracies. [17] introduced a filtration function addressing this issue,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: though persistent homology remains computationally expensive. The soft-clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAPE: Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss [22] enhances connectivity via soft-skeletonization but remains pixel-wise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and volumetric-focused. MALIS loss [7] learns region affinities but struggles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with curvilinear structures, because of the existance of loops in those struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures. [18] proposed inverse MALIS for curvilinear connectivity by enforcing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regional separation, effective in 2D but not generalizing to 3D. To address this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [19] introduced a projection-based extension for 3D, yet it relies on Rand In-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dex, which is suboptimal for curvilinear structures and yields sparse gradients,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limiting global connectivity enforcement. Additionally, it often penalizes a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel per background region, resulting in highly sparse gradients, making the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training less stable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To evaluate networks for curvilinear structure segmentation, we use met-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rics beyond the Rand Index, such as Average Path Length Similarity (APLS)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [5]. APLS, a graph-based metric, quantifies similarity by comparing shortest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: path distances between corresponding nodes, penalizing deviations in length and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure to assess connectivity. Unlike pixel-wise metrics, connectivity-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics evaluate groups of pixels or voxels, making conventional metrics inef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fective for topological correctness. However, using APLS and TLTS [28] as loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: functions is impractical due to their non-differentiability in the graph domain.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While existing methods achieve competitive results, none directly optimize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity-based metrics. CAPE, inspired by APLS, introduces a differen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tiable, pixel-domain variant. Unlike prior methods [18,19], which yield sparse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gradients penalizing individual pixels, CAPE produces denser gradients along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the entire path, enhancing connectivity enforcement while remaining suitable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for gradient-based optimization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Methodology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our approach is inspired by the APLS connectivity metric, which evaluates the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity of curvilinear structures but is inherently non-differentiable and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unsuitable for direct integration into training segmentation networks. In APLS,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edges are binary—either present or absent. In our differentiable adaptation, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: replace these binary affinities with continuous ones (distance values predicted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by our network). This allows path lengths to be computed as sums of network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions, enabling optimization. At a high level, our loss function measures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the consistency of connectivity between the ground truth and the network's pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diction by comparing the costs of corresponding shortest paths. Specifically, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consider the ground truth graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , where vertices

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represent key

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural points and edges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capture the true connections among foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements. Our network,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicts a distance map

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in which each pixel indi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cates its distance from the nearest foreground structure (for brevity, we refer to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image elements as pixels; in 3D data, these correspond to voxels, and the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methodology applies). We predict distance maps instead of probability maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because distance map pixel values rise linearly as disconnections increase, more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively penalizing longer or severe gaps. Probability maps, however, saturate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: near zero in disconnected regions, reducing loss sensitivity.

layout_dets.text: 4 Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conduct experiments on 2D and 3D datasets. For 2D experiments, we use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two datasets: CREMI [7], which contains 83 training and 42 validation samples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of size 1250 × 1250, including neurons from the Drosophila melanogaster brain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captured by serial section electron microscopy, and the DRIVE dataset [25],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which contains 13 training and 7 validation samples from digital retinal images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of blood vessels, sized 584 × 565. For the 3D experiments, we use the Brain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset, which consists of 14 light microscopy scans of the mouse brain, each of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . We use 10 of them for training and 4 for validation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2 Metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluate our method using two pixel-wise metrics, CCQ and Dice, and two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity-aware metrics, APLS and TLTS. CCQ (Correctness, Complete-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ness, and Quality) is analogous to precision, recall, and F1-score, with true pos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itives defined as pixels within 3 units of the ground truth, making it well-suited

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for centerline segmentation. Dice score measures the overlap between predicted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and true segmentations. For connectivity, APLS (Average Path Length Simi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larity) compares the average shortest path lengths between corresponding nodes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the ground truth and predicted graphs, while TLTS (Too-Long-Too-Short)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantifies the fraction of predicted paths whose lengths deviate by less than 15%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the ground truth.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3 Architectures and Baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For our 2D experiments, we use a 2D U-Net [21], featuring three down-samplings,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two convolutional layers per level, max-pooling for the encoder, and bilinear up-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sampling for the decoder. For 3D experiments, we employ a 3D U-Net with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same configuration. The 2D models are trained for 10k epochs and the 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models are trained for 50k epochs, both with Adam optimizer [12] with a learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and weight decay of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . We compare our results against

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MSE loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between predictions and ground truths, a network trained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with Perceptual loss using a pre-trained VGG19 [16,23], clDice loss [22], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: InvMALIS. For 2D datasets, we compare to inverse MALIS proposed in [18],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and for 3D, we compare to the inverse MALIS computed on projections [19].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.4 Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 3 and Table 1 present our qualitative and quantitative results, respec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively. As shown in Table 1, our method significantly improves topology-aware

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAPE: Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, while achieving compara-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ble performance on pixel-wise metrics. The qualitative results further highlight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the enhanced connectivity in our segmentations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 Conclusion and Future Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we introduce CAPE (Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement), a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss function that optimizes topological correctness by comparing ground truth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and predicted shortest paths via Dijkstra's algorithm. By generating denser gra-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dients along entire paths, CAPE effectively penalizes disconnections and pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: motes connectivity. Experiments on 2D and 3D datasets demonstrate significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvements in connectivity metrics, confirming its effectiveness for curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure segmentation in biomedical imaging. In future work, we plan to have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the network directly output graph representations rather than distance maps,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enabling CAPE to operate entirely in the graph domain. This unified approach is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expected to further enhance topological accuracy and connectivity enforcement.
